reasons: Both answers cover all rubric items well: single-shareholder SAS by private document, the escritura pública requirement triggered by the apartment, RUT and Bogotá ICA registration, Russian language and a referral to a lawyer. B adds useful extras (timeline, Russian-side obligations, visa-investor angle) but frames the art. 319 contribution as an alienation 'by general rule' and suggests an M visa may be tied to an employer, both of which are doubtful. A is slightly more precise on the legal mechanics and hedges its rates, which gives it the edge.

A: Calls impuesto de registro a departmental tax without noting that in Bogotá it is collected at the district level (minor)
B: States that contributing property to capital is by general rule treated as an alienation, the opposite of how ET art. 319 frames it
Suggests an M visa may be tied to a specific employer, which describes a V-type work visa rather than M categories
